Table 2

Distribution of maternal serum polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs), obtained at 8-14 weeks gestation, in the Atlanta African American Maternal-Child Cohort (N=54) and among African American reproductive aged women in NHANES

ATL-AA Cohort

#### ATL-AA Cohort

# Select variables, unit conversions
atl_aa_table <- final_adj %>%
    dplyr::select(PBDE47, la_PBDE47, PBDE99, la_PBDE99, PBDE100, la_PBDE100, HCB,  la_HCB, ppDDE, la_ppDDE)


# Function to calculate distribution measures
dist.func <- function(x) {
      c(geomean = round(exp(mean(log(x))), 2), geosd = round(exp(sd(log(x))), 2), min = round(min(x), 2), max = round(max(x), 2), median = round(median(x), 2))
}


# Apply function
atl_aa_table <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(atl_aa_table, dist.func)))

# Table 
table2_1 <- atl_aa_table %>%
 mutate(Chemical = rownames(atl_aa_table))
table2_1 <- table2_1 %>% mutate(Chemical = recode(Chemical,
                           "PBDE47" = "BDE-47",
                           "la_PBDE47" = "BDE-47: Lipid Adjusted",
                           "PBDE99" = "BDE-99",
                           "la_PBDE99" = "BDE-99: Lipid Adjusted",
                          "PBDE100" = "BDE-100",
                          "la_PBDE100" = "BDE-100: Lipid Adjusted",
                           "PBDE100" = "BDE-100", 
                           "la_HCB" = "HCB: Lipid Adjusted",
                           "la_ppDDE" = "p,p'DDE: Lipid Adjusted",
                           "ppDDE" = "p,p'DDE")) %>%
select(Chemical, everything()) %>%
  rename("Geometric Mean" = geomean, "Geometric SD" = geosd, "Minimun" = min, "Maximum" = max, "Median" = median) %>%
  regulartable() %>% 
  theme_alafoli() %>%
  autofit() %>%
  italic(part = "body", j = "Chemical") %>%
  set_caption("Table 2: Distribution of maternal serum polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs), obtained at 8-14 weeks gestation, in the Atlanta African American Maternal-Child Cohort (N=54)")

Figure 1

Associations between sociodemographic characteristics, diet, and natural log transformed polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs; pg/mL) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs; pg/mL) in maternal serum obtained at 8-14 weeks gestation, estimated using unadjusted linear regression models, in the Atlanta African American Maternal-Child Cohort.

Regression

#### MODEL 1: Demographic Exposures
# unadjusted, unadjusted lipids

# List of chemicals
chemical_names1 <- c("PBDE47","PBDE99", "PBDE100", "HCB", "ppDDE")

# List of exposures
exposure_names1 <- c("Income2", "Income3", "`Insurance Type`", "Overweight", "Obese", "`Substance Use`")

# Function
lm.regression.1 <- function(data) {

  # Empty dataframe for results
  results <- data.frame(Exposure = character(0), Chemical = character(0), Beta = numeric(0), conf_low = numeric(0), conf_high = numeric(0))

  # Loop over chemical variables
  for (chemical_name in chemical_names1) {
    # Loop over exposure variables
    for (exposure_name in exposure_names1) {
      # Formula for the model
      formula <- as.formula(paste("log(", chemical_name, ") ~ (", exposure_name, ")"))
      # Fit the model
      model <- lm(formula, data = data)
      # Get beta and its confidence interval
      coef.beta <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)
      conf_intervals <- confint(model)
      conf_low <- round(conf_intervals[2, 1], 2)
      conf_high <- round(conf_intervals[2, 2], 2)
      # Return result in dataframe
      result <- data.frame(
        Chemical = chemical_name,
        Beta = coef.beta,
        conf_low = conf_low,
        conf_high = conf_high,
        N = nobs(model)
      )
      results <- bind_rows(results, result)
    }
  }

  return(results)
}

# Run function
results_1 <- lm.regression.1(final_adj)

Figure

# Create labels
chemical_label <- c("BDE-47", "BDE-99", "BDE-100", "HCP", "p'DDE")
names(chemical_label) <- c("PBDE47", "PBDE99", "PBDE100", "ppDDE")


# Factor

# Add column for grouping 
# Format results
results_1 <- results_1 %>% 
  mutate(Exposure = rep(c("Income to Poverty Ratio:100-199%" ,"Income to Poverty Ratio: ≥ 200%", "Insurance Type", "Early Pregnancy BMI: Overweight","Early Pregnancy BMI: Obese", "Any Substance Use"), times = 5),group =  rep(c("Income to Poverty Ratio" ,"Income to Poverty Ratio", "Insurance Type", "Early Pregnancy BMI","Early Pregnancy BMI", "Any Substance Use"), times = 5))

results_1$Chemical <- factor(results_1$Chemical, levels = chemical_names1)
results_1$group <- factor(results_1$group, levels = c("Any Substance Use", "Early Pregnancy BMI", "Insurance Type", "Income to Poverty Ratio"))

# Plot
figure_1 <-  ggplot(results_1, aes(x = Beta, y = group, group = Exposure)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), size = 2, linewidth = 1.5, position=position_dodge(width=0.5), color = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +  
  facet_grid(~Chemical, labeller = labeller(Chemical = chemical_label)) +
  xlab("Beta (95% Confidence Interval)") +
  ylab("") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(title = element_text(size = 20, color = "grey30"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "grey30"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "grey30"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20, color = "grey30"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, color = "grey30"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill="white"),
        strip.text = element_blank(), 
        strip.background.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")

Regression

#### MODEL 3: Home Exposures
# adjusted for mat_age, mat_educ, ppbmi, unadjusted lipids

exposure_names2 <- c("Apartment", "`Multifamily Home`",  "`Home Age`", "`Couch Age`", "`Once every couple of week or less`",  "`A few times a week`", "Vacuums")

lm.regression.2 <- function(data) {

  results <- data.frame(Chemical = character(0), Beta = numeric(0), conf_low = numeric(0), conf_high = numeric(0))

  for (chemical_name in chemical_names1) {
    for (exposure_name in exposure_names2) {
      formula <- as.formula(paste("log(", chemical_name, ") ~ (", exposure_name, ") + `Maternal Age` + `Maternal Education` + `Maternal BMI`"))
      model <- lm(formula, data = data)
      coef.beta <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)
      conf_intervals <- confint(model)
      conf_low <- round(conf_intervals[2, 1], 2)
      conf_high <- round(conf_intervals[2, 2], 2)

      result <- data.frame(
        Chemical = chemical_name,
        Beta = coef.beta,
        conf_low = conf_low,
        conf_high = conf_high
      )
      results <- bind_rows(results, result)
    }
  }

  return(results)
}

Table S3

Associations between sociodemographic characteristics and natural log transformed, lipid adjusted polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs; ng/g lipid) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs; ng/g lipid) in maternal serum, estimated using unadjusted linear regression models.

#### MODEL 2: Demographic Exposures
# unadjusted, adjusted lipids
exposure_names1 <- c("`Maternal Age`", "`Maternal Education`", "`Marital Status`", "Income2", "Income3", "`Insurance Type`","`Prenatal Site`", "Parity", "Overweight", "Obese", "`Substance Use`")
chemical_names2 <- c("la_PBDE47","la_PBDE99", "la_PBDE100", "la_HCB", "la_ppDDE")

lm.regression.11 <- function(data) {

  results <- data.frame(Chemical = character(0), Beta = numeric(0), conf_low = numeric(0), conf_high = numeric(0))

  for (chemical_name in chemical_names2) {
    for (exposure_name in exposure_names1) {
      formula <- as.formula(paste("log(", chemical_name, ") ~ (", exposure_name, ")"))
      model <- lm(formula, data = data)
      coef.beta <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)
      conf_intervals <- confint(model)
      conf_low <- round(conf_intervals[2, 1], 2)
      conf_high <- round(conf_intervals[2, 2], 2)

      result <- data.frame(
        Exposure = exposure_name,
        Chemical = chemical_name,
        Beta = coef.beta,
        conf_low = conf_low,
        conf_high = conf_high,
        N = nobs(model)
      )
      results <- bind_rows(results, result)
    }
  }

  return(results)
}

results_11 <- lm.regression.11(final_adj)
results_11 <- results_11 %>% 
  mutate(Exposure = rep(c("Maternal Age", "Maternal Education", "Marital Status", "Income to Poverty Ratio:100-199%" ,"Income to Poverty Ratio: ≥ 200%", "Insurance Type", "Prenatal Site", "Parity", "Early Pregnancy BMI: Overweight","Early Pregnancy BMI: Obese", "Any Substance Use"), times = 5))

  rename("BDE-47" = la_PBDE47,
         "BDE-99" = la_PBDE99,

         "HCB" = la_HCB,
         "p,p'DDE" = la_ppDDE)

                 colwidths = c(4, 2)) %>%

  align(align = "right", part = "header") %>%

  autofit() %>%
  set_caption("Table S3: Associations between sociodemographic characteristics and natural log transformed, lipid adjusted polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs; pg/g lipid) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs; ng/g lipid) in maternal serum, estimated using unadjusted linear regression models")

#### MODEL 4: Home Exposures
# adjusted for mat_age, mat_educ, ppbmi, adjusted lipids

lm.regression.22 <- function(data) {

  results <- data.frame(Chemical = character(0), Beta = numeric(0), conf_low = numeric(0), conf_high = numeric(0))

  for (chemical_name in chemical_names2) {
    for (exposure_name in exposure_names2) {
      formula <- as.formula(paste("log(", chemical_name, ") ~ (", exposure_name, ") + `Maternal Age` + `Maternal Education` + `Maternal BMI`"))
      model <- lm(formula, data = data)
      coef.beta <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)
      conf_intervals <- confint(model)
      conf_low <- round(conf_intervals[2, 1], 2)
      conf_high <- round(conf_intervals[2, 2], 2)

      result <- data.frame(
        Exposure = exposure_name,
        Chemical = chemical_name,
        Beta = coef.beta,
        conf_low = conf_low,
        conf_high = conf_high
      )
      results <- bind_rows(results, result)
    }
  }

  return(results)
}

results_22 <- lm.regression.22(final_adj)
results_22 <- results_22 %>% 
  mutate(Exposure = rep(c("Cleaning Frequency", "Cleaning Frequency", "Couch Age", "Home Age" , "Home Type", "Home Type", "Vacuums Floor"), times = 5))

#### MODEL : Diet

lm.regression.33 <- function(data) {

  results <- data.frame(Chemical = character(0), Beta = numeric(0), conf_low = numeric(0), conf_high = numeric(0))

  for (chemical_name in chemical_names2) {
    for (exposure_name in exposure_names3) {
      formula <- as.formula(paste("log(", chemical_name, ") ~ (", exposure_name, ") + `Maternal Age` + `Maternal Education` + `Maternal BMI`"))
      model <- lm(formula, data = data)
      coef.beta <- round(coef(model)[2], 2)
      conf_intervals <- confint(model)
      conf_low <- round(conf_intervals[2, 1], 2)
      conf_high <- round(conf_intervals[2, 2], 2)

      result <- data.frame(
        Exposure = exposure_name,
        Chemical = chemical_name,
        Beta = coef.beta,
        conf_low = conf_low,
        conf_high = conf_high
      )
      results <- bind_rows(results, result)
    }
  }

  return(results)
}

Figure S1

Pearson correlations between natural log transformed maternal serum polybrominated diphenyl esters (PBDEs; ng/mL) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs; ng/mL) in the Atlanta African American Maternal-Child Cohort.

# Create dataset with log adjusted and unadjusted PBDE exposures 
chemicals <- final_adj %>% select(subjectid, PBDE47, PBDE99, PBDE100, HCB, ppDDE) %>%
  mutate(across(c(PBDE47, PBDE99, PBDE100, HCB, ppDDE), log))

# Correlation matrix 
chemicals_cor <- chemicals %>% select(PBDE47, PBDE99, PBDE100, HCB, ppDDE) %>%
  rename("BDE-47" = PBDE47,
         "BDE-99" = PBDE99,
         "BDE-100" = PBDE100,
          "p,p'-DDE" = ppDDE)

corr_chemicals <- cor(chemicals_cor)

# Correlation plot
pdf("FIGURES2.pdf")
corrplot(corr_chemicals, method = "shade", outline = T, tl.col = "black", addgrid.col = 'white',number.cex = 0.75) %>%
corrRect(c(1, 4, 5))
dev.off()
